<reflection>
The three experiments conducted so far have provided data under varying substrate and catalyst concentrations, but all without initial product. The fitting results show that mechanism M7 (substrate inhibition via catS2) consistently has the lowest NLL, but the differences among many mechanisms remain very small (ΔNLL < 0.1 for a large group). This indicates that the data is not yet sufficient to clearly discriminate among the candidates. The aim of the third experiment (high substrate, low catalyst) was to probe saturation effects, which may have slightly favored M7, but further discrimination is needed. To reduce uncertainty over the entire set, we need to introduce a new dimension: the effect of product. Many mechanisms involve product inhibition (e.g., M12, M17) or reversible steps that would be sensitive to product concentration. By adding initial product, we can test these aspects and potentially separate mechanisms that are product-sensitive from those that are not.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
I propose an experiment with moderate substrate (2.0 M), moderate catalyst (0.01 M), and a moderate initial product concentration (0.2 M). This condition directly compares with run1 (same S and cat but no product), allowing us to isolate the effect of product on the kinetics. Mechanisms with explicit product inhibition (e.g., M12: P+cat=>inactive_catP; M17: P+catS=>inactive_catSP) will likely show slower initial rates due to inhibition. Reversible mechanisms (e.g., M1, M2) will have a reduced net forward rate due to the reverse reaction being more significant. In contrast, mechanisms without product sensitivity (e.g., irreversible deactivation or activation) may be less affected. This design avoids extreme conditions and targets a broad range of mechanisms simultaneously, as product sensitivity is a feature that varies across the candidate set. By comparing progress curves with and without initial product, we can gain insights into reversibility and inhibition, thereby narrowing down the plausible mechanisms.
</hypothesis>
